title: Philadelphia Phillies Poach Veteran Catcher From NL East Rival

Philadelphia Phillies Poach Veteran Catcher From NL East Rival

 Aaron Doster-Imagn Images Aaron Doster-Imagn Images Philadelphia Phillies Poach Veteran Catcher From NL East Rival
 Matthew Schmidt Partner Nov 11, 2026 3:40 AM Published Nov 11, 2026 3:40 AM The Philadelphia Phillies have stolen a veteran catcher from an NL East rival.
 More Videos The Philadelphia Phillies entered the offseason in need of some help at catcher, especially after cutting ties with Garrett Stubbs .
 And while the Phillies have been pitched as a potential destination for Carson Kelly , they have decided to settle on a much cheaper backstop for now.
 In the middle of the GM meetings, Philadelphia signed former Miami Marlins catcher Brian Navarreto to a minor-league contract, via Ari Alexander of 7 News .
 Navarreto has spent very little time in the big leagues.
 Related stories
 Now 31 years old, he made his MLB debut with the Marlins back in 2020, playing two games that season. He then toiled away in the minor leagues for the next four seasons before resurfacing in 2025, when he appeared in eight contests.
 This past year, Navarreto participated in 32 games for Miami, slashing .135/.193/.250 with one home run and three RBI. Over 81 plate appearances throughout his limited major-league career, Navarreto owns a .559 OPS.
 Navarreto's selling point is his defense, as evidenced by his three defensive runs saved in just 165.2 innings behind the plate in 2026.
 The veteran has a tremendous arm and is very good at controlling the run game as a result, and he is a decent framer.
 Of course, this surely can't be the only catching addition for the Phillies unless they were just looking for a reincarnation of Stubbs.
 Philadelphia needs offense behind the plate, especially if it is going to be resting J.T. Realmuto more next season (and Dave Dombrowski already said that giving Realmuto more time off is in the plans).
 Realmuto himself was awful at the dish this past season, slashing .205/.283/.331 with 11 home runs and 51 RBI across 467 trips to the plate. He wasn't great in 2025, either, managing a .700 OPS through 550 plate appearances.
 That's why Kelly has been floated as a potential option for the Phillies, as he has been a decent hitter for the Chicago Cubs the last couple of seasons.
 Another possibility is Tyler Stephenson, who spent the first seven years of his big-league career with the Cincinnati Reds and is now on the open market.
 Philadelphia definitely has to do something to address its putrid offense from the catcher position. It also needs to add at least one bat in the outfield, an infielder, multiple relievers and some starting pitching depth.
 As you can see, it should be a busy offseason for the Phillies.
